title: Add an angle of rotation field to widget edit mode for accessibility
line: A rotated desktop widget gets a Reset Rotation button in its edit handle, and holding Shift while rotating snaps to 15° steps.
explanation: Desktop widgets can be rotated freely from the rotate button in their edit handle, which only snaps to 0/90/180/270 within 4 degrees. A widget rotated by accident, easy with limited fine motor control, could only be straightened by another precise drag, and there was no way to rotate to tidy angles. The handle now shows a Reset Rotation button whenever the widget is rotated, which puts it back to 0 with one click and saves it, and holding Shift while dragging the rotate button snaps the angle to 15° steps.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: add Reset Rotation button and Shift snapping

A widget rotated by accident could only be brought back with a precise
drag on the rotate handle. Add a Reset Rotation button to the handle of
rotated widgets, and snap the angle to 15° steps while Shift is held.

BUG: 517492

media.caption: Master: a widget rotated by accident; the handle only offers the free-drag rotate button
Fixed: the rotated widget's handle has a Reset Rotation button; one click puts it back straight
Master: dragging the rotate button gives any angle (here about 20°)
Fixed: dragging the rotate button with Shift held moves in 15° steps (30° to 60°)

reviews.text: Adding a contextual Reset Rotation button (shown only when a desktop widget is rotated) and Shift-key snapping to 15° steps cleanly solves the accidental-rotation accessibility problem without bloating the narrow edit handle with a spin box. The QML diff is minimal, idiomatic, keyboard-accessible, properly localized, and well verified by the before/after media.

The reporter's actual problem is that an accidentally rotated widget can't be snapped back without fine motor control, and they suggested modifier-key snapping as in vector editors; a one-click Reset Rotation button that only appears on rotated widgets plus Shift-snapping to 15° (which includes the 90° steps they mentioned) solves that more simply than a spin-box field in the narrow handle, so it reasonably closes the wish despite the title wording. The change is small and contained to ConfigOverlay.qml: the snap expression wraps 360 to 0 correctly, plain drags keep the old 0/90/180/270 magnet, and reset saves through the same layout.save() path as a drag release. Screenshots and the video frames show the reset button, the new tooltip and Shift-stepped rotation. Nitpick: the edit-reset icon looks a lot like the rotate icon just above it, and the MR text should explain why it's a reset button and not an angle field so maintainers can weigh it.
